newsitem.title: UK: UK STUDENT LOAN SALE COMPLETION LIKELY IN FEB '98.
newsitem.headline: UK STUDENT LOAN SALE COMPLETION LIKELY IN FEB '98.

text.p: Britain's sale of a 1.6 billion stg ($2.5 billion) portfolio of student loans is likely to be completed in February 1998, an advisor to the government said on Monday.

"A shortlist of buyers will be selected by the end of the year, and we would move forward to close (the transaction) by February of next year," Charles Keay, director of N M Rothschild & Sons, which is advising the government on the sale, told Reuters.
Earlier, Rothschild said it had identified 20 potential purchasers of the portfolio who would be asked to submit indicative bids by October 3.

The loans, offered under a scheme started in 1990, pay interest at below market rates. It is planned that the portfolio be sold at face value and the government will provide an ongoing subsidy to the buyer.

The sale is part of Britain's drive to shift risk to the private sector. It has already transferred a host of public assets into private hands, including homes owned by the Ministry of Defence and housing loans made by local authorities.

Consortia of banks have bought these assets and issued bonds securitised by their cashflows to finance the deals. Securitisation is also a possible funding method for the buyers or the student loan portfolio.
"Securitisation is an option that purchasers could use to refinance their acquisition," Keay said.
During the 1998/99 financial year, Britain plans to sell a further 1.5 billion stg of student loans.
